rv.q: It is a lively setup which tries to wrestle with intersecting themes of race, gender and privilege, with dynamic direction from Roy Alexander Weise and lovely a cappella interludes.
Overstretched drama about racism and identity politics at an Ivy League college

The pushing of boundaries and being unafraid to promote strong responses from complex themes shows that the production is bold and compelling, never wavering on whether something is too extreme to include.
The acappella vocals elevate what is already a wonderful theatrical event.
There are some amusing moments, but the show does wear its heart on its sleeve, not always a bad thing, though often the serious aspects of the play seem discordant against the comedy.
Safe Space is a superb debut, and minor caveats can be fixed.
